# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 50 (Bu-Vb Pc50)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc50
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 50
**Title (English, from literature):** Seeing an army in action
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 50, titled *Uyyodhika* ("Seeing an army in action"), is a disciplinary rule in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka governing monastic conduct in the vicinity of armed forces. The rule stipulates that if a monk who is staying with an army goes to observe the army engaged in military action, he incurs an offense of expiation requiring confession (*pācittiya*). An English translation of the text has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Parallel disciplinary injunctions are likewise found in the corresponding nuns' Vinayas, including Theravāda Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 131 and its Chinese and Tibetan equivalents.
